name: Novel / unexplained outbreaks
summary: WHO reported two sporadic MERS cases in Qatar on 13 Nov with no onward spread; no unexplained cluster found
state: WHO reported on 13 Nov that Qatar had notified two laboratory-confirmed MERS cases from August, its first since 2022; all 99 contacts tested negative and WHO found no evidence of sustained human-to-human spread (WHO). MERS is a known pathogen and the cases are sporadic. Searches to 16 Nov found no unexplained cluster under international investigation, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: No action needed beyond routine travel health advice; NaTHNaC publishes outbreak updates for travellers.
rubric_hit: No unexplained clusters under investigation = Normal

sources.title: WHO — Disease Outbreak News: MERS, Qatar

why: The next pandemic will start as an unexplained cluster; early signals matter.
drivers: Surveillance reports, unknown illnesses, new pathogens.

rubric.alert: A novel pathogen with evidence of human-to-human spread across borders.

rubric.normal: No unexplained clusters under international investigation.
